Returned to the client after attempting to activate the account with an email and token. Contains success boolean and a user_status string. Supports detailed UI and workflow handling for multiple verification outcomes.

email.description: User email address to initiate password reset procedure. This must be a valid email and is used as the primary credential for the user in the Todo List system. This property is required to initiate any password reset flow. Multiple requests for non-existent or ineligible accounts yield identical generic responses for security.

ITodoListUser.IResetPasswordRequest.description:
Request schema to initiate a password reset flow for a registered user account. 

Contains the account email which triggers an out-of-band reset-password workflow, if eligibility checks (existence, status) are met. This structure is security-hardened to prevent user enumeration by never indicating whether the email exists in the system. 

If the account is verified, unlocked, and not deleted, a reset_password_token and reset_password_sent_at will be generated and linked to the user, and a notification sent. Otherwise, the response is generic and does not reveal eligibility.

success.description: Always true. Indicates that the reset password process has been started according to policy. The value is deliberately generic to avoid user information leakage.

ITodoListUser.IResetPasswordRequestResul.description:
Response schema for a password reset request operation on the todo_list_users table.

For privacy reasons, this structure always returns success, regardless of whether the provided email exists or the account is eligible for reset. This prevents attackers from inferring the existence or status of user accounts in the system. Used to provide a constant, generic reply to clients in compliance with security requirements.

ITodoListUser.IResetPassword.description:
Password reset request DTO for registered users in the Todo List application.

Used for submitting a password reset with a valid reset_password_token and a new password for the account recovery process. On valid token and compliant new password, resets the user's password and wipes the used token and associated metadata. Response to this DTO results in updating todo_list_users' password_hash and revoking all sessions.

The password field is required; the backend hashes and stores it according to security policy. The reset_password_token must be an exact match for the user's latest reset token, and must not be expired.

The request enforces password policy requirements (minimum 8 characters, must include both a letter and a number). No authentication is performed for this endpoint, and responses are generic to prevent information leakage.

reset_password_token.description: Password reset token issued to the user via email or reset flow. Must exactly match the token in the user's record. Required and must be valid and unexpired. Provided as-is in request body for verification.

password.description: New plain text password to set for the account. Required and must adhere to security policy: at least 8 characters, including at least 1 letter and 1 number. The backend hashes this value before storage in password_hash. Password is never returned in responses.

ITodoListUser.IResetPasswordResult.description:
Password reset result DTO for the Todo List application.

Represents the outcome of an attempted password reset operation. Indicates whether the reset was successful or failed (e.g., invalid/expired token) in a generic, non-leaking way. Designed so the API never reveals whether a password reset token or email is valid to prevent enumeration attacks.

Used for response to ITodoListUser.IResetPassword requests, regardless of success.

Provides an is_success flag for client-side handling, and always supplies a message (which should be generic in case of error).

is_success.description: Indicates whether the password reset operation completed successfully. True if password was set, old tokens revoked, and the account is now recoverable with the new password. False if there was an invalid/expired token or the reset failed. Should not reveal the nature of failure to prevent leaking information about account existence or token validity.

message.description: A human-readable, non-specific message describing the result of the password reset operation. Should not disclose token validity, account existence, or any security-sensitive details. Used for user notification in all cases.

email.description: User email address used for login and identity confirmation during unlock. Must exactly match the registered email for the account that is locked. Required for verification and business rule validation as specified for the unlock process.

unlock_token.description: Token or secret for unlocking the locked user account. Typically sent by email (via previous verification or password reset request), or generated by admin/manual process depending on unlock business logic. Used to authenticate and authorize account unlock.

ITodoListUser.IUnlock.description:
Unlock process request schema for a locked user account in the Todo List system.

This schema includes credential fields required to validate and process the unlock workflow. Unlock operations require the registered email and a valid unlock token or code, which may be generated through email verification, password reset flow, admin intervention or other secure method.

On success, the user's locked status is cleared and their account may be accessed again, subject to business rules defined for account recovery. All fields are strictly validated to match business and audit requirements. Email must match a unique registered account; unlock_token must be an active, valid unlock code.

success.description: Whether the unlock operation succeeded (account unlocked and available for login). True if account status changed from locked to unlocked; false if unlock failed or credentials were invalid.

message.description: Detailed outcome message explaining the result of the unlock operation. On success, provides confirmation. On failure, provides a reason (e.g., invalid token, already unlocked, expired, etc.).

can_login.description: Whether the user is now eligible to attempt login after the unlock operation. True when the account is fully unlocked and not subject to cooldown; false if more steps are required or lockout remains.

next_step.description: Instruction or step to continue account re-entry or recovery if the unlock was not successful or more action is needed. May indicate password reset flow, cooldown period, or contacting support. Null or omitted if no further action is required.

ITodoListUser.IUnlockResult.description:
Unlock operation result schema for Todo List user account recovery workflows.

This schema is returned after processing an unlock request, and indicates the outcome of the unlock process. The result captures whether the operation succeeded, provides a message for user feedback, and indicates if the user is now eligible to log in. The 'next_step' field may be used to guide the user through remaining recovery workflows if the account cannot be fully unlocked yet.

This schema covers security requirements for account recovery, audit, and user communication in compliance with business rules and user experience standards.

ITodoListUser.description:
Registered user entity for the Todo List application.

Represents an individual account uniquely identified by email in the Todo List system. Used for authentication, account management, and as the actor/owner for all user data. Contains identity, authentication lifecycle markers, user status fields, and all metadata for administrative operations, compliance, and auditability.

Includes all fields required for the full user lifecycle: registration, authentication, verification, password reset flows, lockout and unlock events, and deletion lifecycle. These fields support business logic around secure account management, operational support, and full audit history of identity changes and access states.

The schema enforces business rules such as unique email, strict separation of authentication credentials (password hash never exposed via API), comprehensive account status markers (verification, locked, deleted), and compliance with privacy requirements (fields like tokens and timestamps are null unless in recovery, verification, or administrative flow context).

Excludes sensitive authentication (password hashes) from API responses for security. Fields related to email verification, password reset, and account status are exposed for operational auditing and compliance only for administrative/support actors. Lifecycle timestamps and token fields are included as nullable values and described for their specific business flow usage.

id.description: Unique identifier (UUID) for the user. Serves as the system primary key and stable reference for all user operations. Generated upon registration and remains constant for the entire account lifecycle.

email.description: User email address used as the unique login credential. Must conform to RFC 5322 email standards and is always unique among users. Required for registration, login, password reset, and verification processes.

is_verified.description: Flag indicating if the user's email has been successfully verified. Set to true upon completion of email verification flow, enabling access to full application features.

locked.description: Indicates whether the account is currently locked due to repeated failed login attempts, security incidents, or administrative actions. A locked state prevents all login attempts until unlock flow (manual/admin or business logic) clears the status.

oneOf.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC) when the user account was locked due to authentication failures or administrative actions. Null if not currently locked.

locked_at.description: Timestamp when account was locked, or null if never locked.

oneOf.description: One-time token used for confirming user email verification. Populated during registration or re-verification processes; null if not currently in verification or already verified.

email_verification_token.description: Current email verification token, or null if no active token.

oneOf.description: UTC datetime when the last verification email was sent. Updated for each (re)verification flow; null if never sent or already verified.

email_verification_sent_at.description: When verification email was last sent.

oneOf.description: Unique token used when the user initiates a password reset flow; null if none in progress. Required for safe password resets.

reset_password_token.description: Password reset token for ongoing reset operation, or null if not active.

oneOf.description: Datetime when the last password reset token was issued for this account. Used for expiration and audit support; null if never initiated.

reset_password_sent_at.description: When password reset was last triggered.

created_at.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC) when the user account was created. Populated automatically on registration.

updated_at.description: Timestamp (ISO 8601 UTC) when the user profile or status was last updated. Used to support audit and compliance reporting for administration.

oneOf.description: Timestamp if the user account is scheduled for or has completed deletion. Null if the account is currently active.

deleted_at.description: When user account was deleted/removed, or null if still active.

ITodoListUser.IRequest.description:
Request query schema for searching Todo List users with rich filtering, sorting, and pagination support.

This DTO enables system administrators and internal auditors to efficiently locate user accounts by a range of criteria, including email, account status (locked and/or verified), and registration dates. It underpins protected query endpoints for account management and compliance auditing.

Fields support robust business logic for pagination (page, limit), flexible sorting (sort_by, sort_order), and edge cases such as tight date ranges or highly restrictive filtering. The schema is intended for use in internal systems only—never exposed in public/anonymous API operations.

page.description: Page index for paginated results. The first page is always 1. Exceeding the available number of pages yields a zero-length result set.

limit.description: The number of user records to return per page. Limited to ensure efficient queries (default 20; maximum 100 for admin screens).

email.description:
Exact email address filter: returns only the user with this specific email (case-insensitive). 

Supports account validation and targeted user audits, but never supports partial or fuzzy matching for privacy.

is_verified.description: If provided, will filter users according to their email verification status. True = only verified users, False = only unverified users; omitted = any.

locked.description: If provided, restricts the result set to only users whose account lock status matches this value. True = locked users (temporarily disabled access), False = active/unlocked; omitted = any.

from_date.description: Query boundary: return only users who registered at or after this UTC ISO8601 datetime. Useful for compliance or forensic queries by date of account creation.

to_date.description: Query boundary: return users registered at or before this UTC ISO formatted datetime. Commonly used for admin reports or audit slices.

oneOf.description: Sort by registration/creation date ascending or descending (see sort_order).
Sort by email address order (lexical, case-insensitive).

sort_by.description: Choose which user property to sort on (created_at or email). Only columns explicitly supported are allowed to avoid index performance and security risks.

oneOf.description: Ascending (A-Z or oldest-first) sort.
Descending (Z-A or newest-first) sort.

sort_order.description: Sorting direction for the resulting records (ascending or descending).

ITodoListUser.ISummary.description:
User summary data object for the Todo List application.

This schema provides a distilled view of the user entity, returning only the most fundamental identification data necessary to reference a user in lists and task ownership checks. It is designed to minimize personal data exposure, strictly omitting any authentication or security-sensitive attributes.

Used for embedding user references within todo lists, system search results, and ownership metadata. Is suitable for display in administrative screens and audit logs where extra information would infringe on user privacy or is unnecessary for the use case.

Field selection is intentional: only email (as unique identifier and notification address) and database UUID (for relational linkages) are provided. Excludes status, verification, or security flags, supporting both atomic lookups and GDPR/data minimization requirements.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the user account in the todo_list_users table. System-generated as a UUID v4 value and never reused.

This value is referenced in all relational data, user-owned objects (such as todo items), and administrative links. Ensures global uniqueness and prevents collisions when synchronizing identities across multiple instances or exporting data. Always present in every user summary.

email.description:
User's registered email address, guaranteed unique within the system. 

This email is the primary credential for user authentication, notification delivery, and identity proofing. It is validated for proper email format and ensured unique by database constraints. Visible in administrative overviews and reference objects, but never exposed in contexts requiring higher privacy (such as public listings).

User email address. Must be unique and conform to RFC email standards.

This is a profile field updatable by the user, subject to unique constraints and validation rules.

Cannot be set to null. Value must follow business logic for update operations and will trigger updated_at auditing.

ITodoListUser.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating a registered user's account profile in the Todo List application.

Allows modification of updatable profile fields only. Excludes authentication credentials (password, password hash), system/ownership fields (id, deleted_at), and business logic-forbidden fields (locked, locked_at, is_verified, etc.).

All updates are strictly audited and validated for uniqueness and correct value formats. Ownership fields, authentication credentials, account lifecycles, and status flags are immutable through this DTO. This schema enforces the separation of updateable user-facing data versus system-internal data.

created_at_gte.description: Earliest session creation time to include in the query. Used for filtering session history results by lower bound on creation date.

created_at_lte.description: Latest session creation time to include in the query. Used for filtering session history results by upper bound on creation date.

expired_only.description: Whether to include only expired sessions (true), only active sessions (false), or all (omit for all).

ip_contains.description: Optional filter for searching for sessions initiated from IP addresses containing this search string fragment.

page.description: Page number for paginated results. Must be a positive integer (1-based).

limit.description: Maximum number of session summary entries returned per page. Used for pagination and must be within [1, 100].

oneOf.description: Session sorting order field. Must be one of the fixed allowed values for consistent query and pagination ordering.
Session sorting order field. Must be one of the fixed allowed values for consistent query and pagination ordering.

order_by.description: Session sorting order field. Must be one of the fixed allowed values for consistent query and pagination ordering.

oneOf.description: Sort order for results (ascending or descending by chosen order_by field).
Sort order for results (ascending or descending by chosen order_by field).

order_direction.description: Sort order for results (ascending or descending by chosen order_by field).

user_agent_contains.description: Filter for sessions by user agent substring match (for device OS/browser audits, if available).

ITodoListUserSession.IRequest.description:
Search and filtering DTO for advanced query of session history records associated with a user in the Todo List application.

Allows filtering by creation time range, session expiration status, IP address fragment, and flexible pagination with custom sorting order. This type is used in session query APIs for security audits and login history pages. All fields are optional to allow piecemeal or full-dataset queries as required. This DTO supports both basic and advanced administrators' review scenarios.

ITodoListUserSession.description:
Session and login audit entity for Todo List service.

Represents a concrete instance of a user's authenticated session, providing complete audit and forensic details for login activity, IP tracking, referrer, and session lifecycle. Each session is irrevocably linked to a user via foreign key, with context fields for IP, login endpoint, and referrer required for compliance and detailed auditing. Sessions enforce robust separation for user security and analysis and are not independently creatable by API users—managed via login/logout flows only.

All fields are returned read-only and are essential for security reporting, anomaly detection, and user-forensic queries. Session deletion or modification is only permissible through proper authentication flows (logout, password reset, or account deletion).

id.description: Unique session record identifier. Primary key for the todo_list_user_sessions table.

todo_list_user_id.description: User account identifier to which this session belongs. References {@link todo_list_users.id}. Enforces strict per-user session isolation and partitioning for all audit and security. Never supplied or modifiable from user input.

ip.description: Client IP address from which the session or login was initiated. Used for audit, user alerting, and security monitoring. Must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 literal.

href.description: The full frontend URL, SPA route, or endpoint address seen by the client at login or session creation. Required for complete audit-trails and debugging.

referrer.description: URL referrer at the moment of session creation. May be an empty string for direct accesses or when not applicable. Always required for full context; never null.

created_at.description: UTC timestamp of session creation event. Used for audit, default ordering, and compliance record-keeping.

expired_at.description: Timestamp marking when the session was expired or revoked. Null if session is currently active. Used for logout, session expiry, and audit purposes.

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description:
Query request filter and pagination settings for listing the authenticated user's todo items.

Allows paginated and filtered retrieval using keyword search, completion status, date filtering, and standard paging controls. Business validation is enforced for all filters and limits. This DTO is submitted to the server as the request body for filtered todo list queries supporting user-centric search and list render flows.

Security is handled by backend—this DTO never accepts user_id or any actor-identifying information. Pagination is enforced server-side for performance and to prevent over-fetching. All results are always scoped to current authenticated user only.

All field values are optional unless specified by API. Invalid or out-of-range limits/values are handled gracefully with validation errors.

keyword.description: Optional user-provided search keyword for filtering todo titles or descriptions. If present, must be 1-100 characters.

oneOf.description: Completion status to filter todos: 'complete' for finished tasks, 'incomplete' for unfinished. If omitted, returns both.
Completion status to filter todos: 'complete' for finished tasks, 'incomplete' for unfinished. If omitted, returns both.

status.description: Completion status to filter todos: 'complete' for finished tasks, 'incomplete' for unfinished. If omitted, returns both.

created_from.description: Lower bound (inclusive) filter for todo creation date. Must be ISO 8601 date or datetime format. Optional.

created_to.description: Upper bound (inclusive) filter for todo creation date. Must be ISO 8601 date or datetime format. Optional.

page.description: 1-based page number for paginated results. Defaults to 1. Must be a positive integer.

limit.description: Maximum number of todos to return per page. Defaults to 20. Must be between 1 and 100.

oneOf.description: Sort order for results: newest first ('created_at:desc') or oldest first ('created_at:asc'). Defaults to newest first.
Sort order for results: newest first ('created_at:desc') or oldest first ('created_at:asc'). Defaults to newest first.

order.description: Sort order for results: newest first ('created_at:desc') or oldest first ('created_at:asc'). Defaults to newest first.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary DTO for a todo item as used in list and search views—provides only high-value attributes for overview and optimized performance.

Omits heavy/full properties such as 'description' or 'updated_at', focusing on minimal yet sufficient data for users to identify and distinguish their tasks at-a-glance.

Always references the owner by unique identifier and email via ITodoListUser.ISummary to ensure audit trails and correct partitioning. Used in pagination, search result rows, and filtered overviews. Business logic will never supply fields outside those defined here—this is a strict subset, never a superset, of the full ITodoListTodo entity.

id.description:
Unique identifier (UUID v4) for this todo item, as set in the todo_list_todos Prisma DB table.

Required for distinguishing between rows in any list or search result and for all subsequent detail/view actions.

title.description:
Task title, unique within the user's todo set. Mandatory; up to 100 Unicode characters enforced by the backend DB.

The primary label for user-facing todo listings, optimized for usability in pagination and fast search operations.

oneOf.description: Todo is currently open and actionable.
Todo has been finished by the user.

status.description:
Business completion status of the todo item. Accepts only 'incomplete' or 'complete' (as enforced by backend logic).

Enables quick filtering in overview screens or mobile lists.

completed_at.description:
UTC datetime when the todo was completed. Will be null/unset for tasks not yet finished.

Used for motivating, segmenting, and archiving completed items from list screens.

created_at.description:
UTC timestamp when the todo was originally added to the system.

Allows for ordering by date and age in overview/result UIs.

ITodoListTodo.description:
Represents a single todo item uniquely owned by one authenticated user within the Todo List application.

Provides the canonical structure mapping to the todo_list_todos Prisma table for both database and API response use. Used for returning the complete details of a todo in read, update, and create operations. Captures every field required for auditing, validation, and business functionality.

Each todo is exclusively tied to an owner (todo_list_users) and includes a user summary reference. The model enforces strict ownership: no sharing or transfer is possible. Field validation occurs for title uniqueness and length, optional description constraints, strict status (incomplete/complete, only), and controlled handling of completion and audit timestamps.

All fields directly correspond to column definitions in the Prisma schema; the structure is never extended by virtual fields or implementation artifacts. Deviations from this structure indicate a contract error in the backend or database configuration.

id.description:
Primary Key. Unique identifier for this todo item within the system, generated as a version-4 UUID. Never reused or reassigned.

Required for every read, update, or delete operation. Enforces item uniqueness and supports system-wide traceability of actions.

user.description:
Reference to the summary record of the user who owns this todo. This is a strict foreign key relationship to the todo_list_users table, enforcing single-user ownership.

Ownership is immutable; a todo cannot be reassigned or shared. The summary reference provides just enough identity for audit and context without exposing sensitive fields.

title.description:
Short, unique title of the todo. Required; must be unique within the user's set and limited to a maximum of 100 Unicode characters.

Acts as the primary visible identifier in listings and detail displays. The backend enforces both length and per-user uniqueness for consistency and user experience.

description.description:
Long-form description or extra details for the todo. Optional; if provided, must be 1000 characters or fewer. Null if there is no description.

Intended to allow users to provide extended notes or context for more complex tasks. Backend validation ensures both maximum length and correct null handling.

oneOf.description: Todo has not yet been completed and remains actionable.
Todo is finished and can be filtered from incomplete views.

status.description:
Current business completion status of the todo. Only 'incomplete' or 'complete' values accepted—enforced by the system.

Controls display, filtering, and audit mechanisms for user productivity.

completed_at.description:
Timestamp (in UTC ISO 8601) of when this todo was marked as complete. Null if the item is still open or incomplete.

Used to audit completion events and reset status if the todo is re-activated.

created_at.description:
UTC timestamp marking when this todo was created. Set once at insertion and never updated thereafter.

Used for audit, default sorting, and lifespan analysis of tasks.

updated_at.description:
UTC timestamp recording the most recent update to this todo (content or status change). Set automatically by the backend for every API modification.

Supports full auditing and traceability of all user modifications.

title.description: Title of the todo item. Required; must be unique per user and limited to 100 Unicode characters.

description.description: Optional free-text description (up to 1000 characters) providing additional context for the task. If present, cannot exceed length constraint.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
Payload for creating a new todo item belonging to the authenticated user.

Must include a non-empty, at-most 100 character title, unique within this user's todo list. Description is optional but, if provided, cannot exceed 1000 characters. User ownership is enforced server-side, so ownership fields are not accepted in client requests. Created/updated timestamps and status are managed automatically on the backend.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
Request payload for updating an existing todo item owned by the authenticated user.

Allows modification of title, description, and completion status. Fields are all optional; omitted properties remain unchanged. Field validation ensures title uniqueness (per user), length, and logical status transitions. Ownership is strictly enforced via authentication context, not in payload.

Updates the updated_at timestamp automatically; completion state changes set or clear completed_at accordingly.

title.description: New title of the todo item (if updating). Must remain unique per user and comply with length limits.

description.description: Updated description (if changing). Null to remove description.

oneOf.description: Completion status: set to 'complete' or 'incomplete'. Transitions are validated to update completed_at correctly.
Completion status: set to 'complete' or 'incomplete'. Transitions are validated to update completed_at correctly.

status.description: Completion status: set to 'complete' or 'incomplete'. Transitions are validated to update completed_at correctly.

ITodoListUserSession.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a registered user's login/audit session.

Provides compact session context for security logs, activity monitors, and access tracking, referencing the owning user via .ISummary. Contains only non-sensitive audit/event data required to display a session in lists or summaries.

Excludes full session metadata and never includes JWT or refresh tokens.

id.description: Session identifier. Uniquely identifies a login record/audit event for the owning user session.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the user session was created. Used for chronological sorting and audit display.

expired_at.description: Timestamp when session expired, revoked or was completed. Null if session is still active.

scenario.draft: Test user registration with an email address that is already registered. The system should reject the registration and provide a clear error message indicating the duplicate. This verifies uniqueness constraint and proper error reporting.

dependencies.purpose: Register the email address so it exists for duplicate attempt

scenario.draft: Test login with correct credentials before email verification. Register a new user but do not verify the email. Ensure login attempt is rejected and provides a generic error (no info leak whether it is due to email or password).

dependencies.purpose: Register a new user for unverified login scenario

scenario.draft: Verify that a user's session detail—including login IP, referrer, timestamps, and session validity—can be fetched using a valid userId and sessionId. Confirm the endpoint provides all audit and security fields as described, enforces linkage between user and session, and denies access if session does not belong to the user. No authentication is required for retrieval, but proper filtering and relationship validation are expected.

Test that an authenticated user can create a todo item by supplying a unique title (required, ≤100 chars) and optional description (≤1000 chars/null). Scenario covers successful creation flow, capturing initial status 'incomplete', ownership, and correct timestamp fields. Also validates that duplicate titles within the same user's list are rejected and that missing or invalid title/description are properly handled by business rules. Edge case: title is whitespace or >100 chars, description is too long or null. Only unique titles per user are allowed; other users may have duplicate titles independently.

dependencies.purpose: Authenticate as a new user before attempting to create a todo item.

Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /auth/user/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'user' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'user' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

scenario.draft: Test that a registered user can successfully update their own todo item, modifying any of title, description, or completion status. Ensure updates are subject to length, uniqueness, and allowed values validation. The workflow is: register (join) a user, create a todo (dependency assumed available by test plan context), update the todo item's properties with a valid payload, and verify the returned todo reflects changes as well as audit timestamps. Also validate updating status transitions ('incomplete' to 'complete' and back), and that invalid changes are appropriately rejected.

dependencies.purpose: Register a user to establish authentication for todo ownership and updates.

Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /auth/user/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'user' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'user' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

scenario.draft: Test that a registered user can permanently delete their own todo item. The scenario covers user registration (join), creation of at least one todo (dependency assumed by test plan context), then deletion of the specified todo using its id. Validate that deletion is irreversible, only possible for the owner, and that further attempts to access the now-deleted todo fail with the correct error. Also test that a user cannot delete a todo owned by another user.

dependencies.purpose: Register a user so they can own and delete todos in a secure context.

Essential authentication prerequisite:
This join operation (post /auth/user/join) must be executed before any operations requiring 'user' actor authorization.
It establishes the necessary user account and authentication context for the 'user' actor, enabling subsequent API calls that depend on this specific authorization level.
Without this join operation, the main scenario endpoint and its dependencies will fail due to insufficient authentication credentials.

scenario.draft: Validates the password reset request flow when a user provides a registered and eligible email address. Ensures that a reset token is generated, sent securely via email, and the response does not disclose account existence or eligibility. Checks that rate limiting and generic messaging are enforced to prevent information leakage.

Verifies that submitting a password reset request for a non-existent or ineligible email (deleted/locked accounts) returns an identical generic response as a valid email request. Confirms the service's resistance to enumeration and information disclosure attacks, enforcing system privacy requirements.

Tests resetting a user's password with a valid reset_password_token and a new password that meets policy. Confirms the password is updated, all existing sessions are revoked, and the reset token is wiped. Ensures successful completion and account can log in only with the new password.

Checks password reset behavior when an expired or invalid reset_password_token is supplied along with a new password. Validates that the response is generic and does not indicate whether the failure was due to token validity, and that no state is changed if the reset is not successful.

Validates enforcement of password strength requirements by attempting to reset the password with a value failing minimum length or character class constraints. Confirms the response remains generic to avoid leaking details and that the password is never updated in these cases.

Verify that a user can successfully refresh their JWT access and refresh tokens by providing a valid, active refresh token. The test simulates an authenticated session where the refresh token is active, unexpired, and not revoked. Validates that new tokens are issued and session audit log is updated. Expected result: successful response with new tokens and renewed session state.

Confirm that the refresh endpoint correctly rejects an invalid or expired refresh token. The scenario simulates attempts to refresh using a token that is not associated with an active session, is expired, or has been revoked. Expected result: appropriate error response indicating invalid or unusable refresh token; no changes to session records.

Confirm that the endpoint correctly rejects refresh requests if the user account is currently locked (locked field true or locked_at not null). Simulate a refresh attempt from a locked user session. Expected result: error response indicating user account is locked and tokens are not refreshed.

Verify that token refresh fails for users whose accounts are not verified (is_verified field is false). Simulate a refresh request for an unverified user's active session. Expected result: endpoint returns error and session/tokens are not refreshed.

Verify that a user can successfully activate their account by providing the valid email and verification token after registration.
